items.title: Fine particulate air pollution and hospital admission for cardiovascular and respiratory diseases
items.document: Article PDF, plus any online supplement (eTables)
items.why: Dominici 2006 JAMA is the source cited for 6 Step 1 rows (S1-01/02/03/05/06/07: CVD, respiratory, IHD, CHF, arrhythmia, cerebrovascular). Its cause-specific ICD-9 definitions are the reference set.

items.title: Coarse particulate matter air pollution and hospital admissions for cardiovascular and respiratory diseases among Medicare patients
items.document: Article PDF, plus any online supplement
items.why: Peng 2008 JAMA is cited for S1-01/02/09/11 (CVD, respiratory, COPD, pneumonia/RTI).

items.title: Comprehensive smoking bans and acute myocardial infarction among Medicare enrollees in 387 US counties: 1999–2008
items.document: Article PDF, plus any online supplement
items.why: Barr 2012 (smoking bans) is the source for S1-04, acute MI (ICD-9 410).

items.title: Impact of long-term exposures to ambient PM2. 5 and ozone on ARDS risk for older adults in the United States
items.document: Article PDF, plus any online supplement
items.why: Rhee 2019 is cited for S1-12 (ARDS, ICD-9 518.82). The 2020 Rhee paper (fetched) lists 518.51-518.53 too, so checking the 2019 definition matters.

items.title: Temporal variation in association between short-term exposure to fine particulate matter and hospitalisations in older adults in the USA: a long-term time-series analysis of …
items.why: Chen 2021 is cited for S1-01 (CVD all-cause). Gold open access, so it should download without an account.

items.title: Comparing traditional and causal inference methodologies for evaluating impacts of long-term air pollution exposure on hospitalization with Alzheimer disease and related dementias
items.why: Qin 2024/25 is cited for S1-17 (dementia/Alzheimer's: 290.0, 331.0 / F01-F03, G30).

items.title: Wildfire-specific fine particulate matter and risk of hospital admissions in urban and rural counties
items.why: Liu 2017 wildfire paper (S1-27). The main text says 'The ICD-9 codes of diagnoses are in eAppendix'.

items.title: Medical diagnoses of heat wave-related hospital admissions in older adults
items.why: Hopp 2018 (S1-24 heat stroke / heat illness). The supplement lists the ~50 heat-related ICD-9 diagnoses; the main text names only the CCS groups.

items.title: Cause-specific risk of hospital admission related to extreme heat in older adults
items.why: Bobb 2014 JAMA (S1-24, S1-26 heat multi-cause). The main text uses 283 CCS groups; the supplement should show the categories and codes behind the heat-sensitive outcomes.

items.title: Estimating the effects of fine particulate matter on 432 cardiovascular diseases using multi-outcome regression with tree-structured shrinkage
items.document: Article PDF, plus supplementary material (likely paywalled: JASA)
items.why: Thomas 2020 is cited for S1-13 (cardiorespiratory). Outcome-wide study (432 ICD-9 CVD codes), so its value depends on the pending 2.6 decision on outcome-wide papers. Probably needs a library account.

items.title: A Bayesian multi-outcome analysis of fine particulate matter and cardiorespiratory hospitalizations
items.why: Thomas 2022 (S1-13). The main text already defines outcomes as CCS groups 7.x/8.x; the eAppendix adds the diagnosis list. Outcome-wide.

items.title: Evaluation of the health impacts of the 1990 clean air act amendments using causal inference and machine learning
items.why: Nethery 2021, Clean Air Act (CVD, dementia). The main text says the ICD-9 codes are in Supplement Section 2.2. Not cited in Step 1. Most other supplement files are code (.r/.md).

items.title: PM2. 5 and hospital admissions among Medicare enrollees with chronic debilitating brain disorders
items.why: Yitshak-Sade 2021 (S1-16). The main text already gives the cohort and main cause codes (332, 3310, 290, 486, ...).

items.title: Association of air particulate pollution with bone loss over time and bone fracture risk: analysis of data from two independent studies
items.why: Prada 2017, fracture codes (in Supplementary Table 1). The outcome is not in the Step 1 PDF.

items.title: Epidemiology of cardiac amyloidosis–associated heart failure hospitalizations among fee-for-service medicare beneficiaries in the United States
items.why: Gilstrap 2019, amyloidosis + HF codes (in the Appendix). The outcome is not in the Step 1 PDF.

items.title: Emergency hospital admissions for cardiovascular diseases and ambient levels of carbon monoxide: results for 126 United States urban counties, 1999–2005
Tropical cyclone exposures and risks of emergency Medicare hospital admission for cardiorespiratory diseases in 175 urban United States counties, 1999–2010
Risk of acute respiratory distress syndrome among older adults living near construction and manufacturing sites
items.why: Rhee 2020 (S1-12). Codes are already in the main text (518.51, 518.52, 518.53, 518.82).

items.title: The effect of long-term exposure to air pollution and seasonal temperature on hospital admissions with cardiovascular and respiratory disease in the United States: a difference …
items.why: Danesh Yazdi 2022. ICD-9 and ICD-10 codes are already in the main text.

items.title: Nationwide study of short-term exposure to fine particulate matter and cardiovascular hospitalizations among Medicaid enrollees
items.why: deSouza 2021. Codes are already in the main text.

items.title: Temporal changes in associations between high temperature and hospitalizations by greenspace: analysis in the Medicare population in 40 US northeast counties
items.why: Heo 2021. Codes are already in the main text (CVD ranges, 992.0).

items.title: Impact of National Ambient Air Quality Standards nonattainment designations on particulate pollution and health
items.why: Zigler 2018. Codes are already in the main text (490-492, ...).

items.title: Geographic disparities in the incidence and outcomes of hospitalized myocardial infarction: does a rising tide lift all boats?
items.why: Yeh 2012. MI codes are already in the main text (410.xx except 410.x2).

items.title: National trends in pancreatic cancer outcomes and pattern of care among Medicare beneficiaries, 2000 through 2010
items.why: Wang 2014, pancreatic cancer (157.xx in the main text). Not in the Step 1 PDF.

items.title: Spatial variable selection methods for investigating acute health effects of fine particulate matter components
items.why: Boehm Vock 2015, a methods paper. CVD codes are referenced in the main text.

items.title: Associations between greenness and kidney disease in Massachusetts: The US Medicare longitudinal cohort study
items.why: Lee 2023 Env Int, greenness and kidney disease. Not the EHP paper cited for S1-18 (that one, ehp10729, was fetched). The kidney codes probably match the EHP paper.

items.title: A Bayesian hierarchical distributed lag model for estimating the time course of risk of hospitalization associated with particulate matter air pollution
items.why: Peng 2009 JRSS-C, a methods paper (IHD, COPD). Not the JAMA 2008 paper cited in Step 1.

items.title: Estimating the acute health effects of coarse particulate matter accounting for exposure measurement error
items.why: Chang 2011, a methods paper (cardiovascular). Not cited in Step 1.

items.title: A meta-analysis and multisite time-series analysis of the differential toxicity of major fine particulate matter constituents
items.why: Levy 2012 meta-analysis (cardiovascular). Not cited in Step 1.

items.title: Causal inference methods for estimating long-term health effects of air quality regulations
items.why: HEI 2016 report on causal methods (respiratory). Not cited in Step 1; no DOI.
